text: Johann Caspar Füssli (3 January 1706 – 6 May 1782) was a Swiss portrait painter and art historian. He was born in Zürich to Hans Rudolf Füssli, a painter, and Elisabeth Schärer. Füssli studied painting in Vienna from 1724 to 1731 and subsequently became a portraitist in the courts of southern Germany. In 1736, he returned to Zürich, where he painted members of the government and Enlightenment figures such as Johann Jakob Bodmer and Friedrich Gottlieb Klopstock. He also authored and illustrated two dictionaries of Swiss painters, establishing himself as a recognized art historian. Füssli married Elisabeth Waser and had 18 children; four of them became painters: Johann Heinrich ("Henry Fuseli", 1741–1825), Johann Kaspar (1743–1786), Elisabeth (1744–1780), and Anna (1749–1772). Johann Caspar Füssli died in Zürich in 1782. This article about a Swiss painter is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by adding missing information.
